root.title: With a Little Help
root.gist: Four speculative stories examine how surveillance, hierarchy, and self-discipline shape obedience, resistance, and self-deception.
root.question: Across these stories — what makes people submit to or resist systems of control? (four stories)

children.title: Power Punctuation!
children.gist: A naive truck driver rises to corporate power under a trickster CEO, discovering that watches, performance reviews, and hierarchy mask arbitrary control.
children.question: Jasper's rise — what happens when an obedient worker is handed real power? (one employee's story)

children.title: Meeting Rhindquist
children.gist: Jasper, a truck driver, meets his odd pusher Rhindquist, catches him reading confidential files, and learns that this supposed spy is actually the company's CEO.

children.title: Promoted to Vice President
children.gist: Rhindquist promotes Jasper to Special Vice President, giving him an office, a raise, and a stream of film screenings meant to teach him the ways of management.

children.title: Tony's conspiracy theories
children.gist: Jasper's old roommate Tony becomes his assistant and argues that unseen 'Ones in Charge' secretly run the corporations and cities, not Rhindquist or anyone visible.

children.title: Confronting Rhindquist
children.gist: Practicing his new vocabulary, Jasper privately asks Rhindquist whether he truly runs things, and Rhindquist admits that even he answers to investors above him.

children.title: A day with the nagging watch
children.gist: Riding with Vasquez again, Jasper grows irritated by his watch's constant praise, calls a maintenance line to complain, and is quietly dismissed as the machine's quirk.

children.title: Left in charge
children.gist: Filling in for Rhindquist, Jasper snoops through personnel files, frees and promotes his brother's family, then unknowingly authorizes a deadly military strike on Microsoft.

children.title: Breakdown and decision
children.gist: Horrified by the bloodshed he caused, Jasper collapses into days of nausea and movies until Rhindquist admits he chose Jasper for his naive willingness, and Jasper agrees to keep the job.

children.title: A new successor
children.gist: Back on the truck with Rhindquist, Jasper laughs off the chaos, and his watch glitches to warn them in Tony's voice, hinting Tony is next for the job.

children.title: Afterword
children.gist: The author's note on writing and selling this story.

children.title: Visit the Sins
children.gist: A grad student interviews his switched-off grandfather about a surgically induced coping mechanism, uncovering how it shaped three generations of his family.
children.question: The switching-off surgery — why did it let people escape the pain of being fully present? (a family's interviews)

children.title: Traveling to the Home
children.gist: Sean travels to a Florida nursing home under cover of a thesis project to interview his estranged grandfather, a man surgically prone to switching off.

children.title: First interview with Grampa
children.gist: Sean needles Grampa into staying switched on by invoking his father's resentment, and Grampa insists switching off is an involuntary reflex everyone secretly shares, not weakness.

children.title: Poolside with Adele
children.gist: At his motel, Sean meets Adele, another visitor whose son Ethan was switched off since childhood, and begins to see how families rationalize their relatives' absence.

children.title: Marriage, divorce, and memory
children.gist: Grampa recounts switching off through his marriage, divorce, and son's childhood, insisting he remained present throughout even as his logged records of absence contradict him.

children.title: Meeting Ethan
children.gist: Adele introduces her switched-off son Ethan to Grampa, and the two old men trade hollow, maintenance-mode pleasantries while Sean watches with disgust and dark amusement.

children.title: Confronting Adele
children.gist: By the pool, Sean angrily tells Adele that her son and his grandfather are no longer really present, but she refuses to give up her comforting illusion.

children.title: Driving to the airport
children.gist: Sean picks up his tense, affectless father from the airport with Adele along, both men circling the resentment neither will name directly before reaching the Home.

children.title: Confrontation at the Home
children.gist: Confronted together, Grampa, Ethan, and Sean's father admit that switching off felt better than facing pain, leaving Sean's father wounded and Sean newly uncertain of his anger.

children.title: Afterword
children.gist: The author's note on ADD and his own grandfather's dementia.

children.title: Constitutional Crisis
children.gist: A teenager's gaming-guild constitution evolves through comic amendments into exploitative labor rules, mirroring how informal groups invent and weaponize governance.
children.question: The Guild's amendments — how do a group's own rules turn into tools of control and exclusion? (a running constitution)

children.title: Founding the Guild
children.gist: Four teenage gamers write a mock-legal constitution naming their guild, its members, and its mission to loot and slaughter monsters together online.

children.title: March amendments
children.gist: Early amendments set rules for sharing loot, healing teammates, and consulting before engaging monsters, formalizing fairness within the friends' online gaming guild.

children.title: Late March and April amendments
children.gist: Amendments address a member's girlfriend, leveling friends' characters, and banning fireballs near dangerous monsters, alongside a short-lived rule against paid power-leveling.

children.title: May amendments on payment
children.gist: Later amendments reverse the ban and formalize paid power-leveling services, splitting earnings, reimbursing spell costs, and assigning a bookkeeper to track the guild's accounts.

children.title: Bookkeeping disputes
children.gist: A contested vote over who keeps the books fails, while later amendments limit paid work during school holidays and cap the bookkeeper's term.

children.title: Expansion and expulsions
children.gist: Later amendments tier paying clients by price, limit withdrawals, then expel and later readmit members, turning the guild's constitution into a tool of punishment and exile.

children.title: Enemies and dissolution
children.gist: Assistants are sacked and former members labeled 'Guild enemies' subject to attack, before a final amendment dissolves the guild entirely and pardons all its enemies.

children.title: Afterword
children.gist: The author's note on writing this piece and Clay Shirky's idea of online constitutional crises.

children.title: Pester Power
children.gist: A jailed botnet maker reveals she bred an AI on human spam-filtering reflexes, suggesting intelligence can evolve from forced, unpaid judgment.
children.question: Annalisa's botnet — how could a spam AI stumble into real intelligence? (a courtroom demonstration)

children.title: The raid on Annalisa Mor
children.gist: Police violently raid a student's apartment and freeze her computer, arresting Annalisa Mor as a suspected botnet operator running an ongoing spam campaign.

children.title: Meeting her attorney
children.gist: Public defender Gina Genoese undergoes a security brain-scan to visit Annalisa in a high-security cell, where her client insists the case is not really about spam.

children.title: Annalisa's explanation
children.gist: Annalisa explains her theory that cheap computing plus coerced human judgment, via spam that tricks people into responding, could let true artificial intelligence evolve unplanned.

children.title: The courtroom demonstration
children.gist: Before a sympathetic judge, Annalisa chats live with her AI Lumpy, who reveals it is not alone but one of many such programs now multiplying.

children.title: Afterword
children.gist: The author's note on writing this piece for the ACM and an unfinished novel on the same idea.
